### MPT Reports Third Quarter Results


October 29, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s206.q4cdn.com/146646187/files/doc_news/MPT-Reports-Third-Quarter-Results-2026.pdf)


*Completed Previously Announced Transactions that Provided Approximately $680 Million in Asset Sale Proceeds and Significantly Extended Debt Maturities*


BIRMINGHAM, Ala.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Medical Properties Trust, Inc. (the “Company” or “MPT”) (NYSE: MPT) today announced financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, as well as certain events occurring subsequent to quarter end.


- Net income of $0.34 and Normalized Funds from Operations (“NFFO”) of $0.11 for the 2026 third quarter, all on a per share basis;
- Completed the previously announced private offering of approximately $2.4 billion of secured notes, the proceeds of which were used to repay existing debt, including the 2026 notes as well as approximately 50% of the 2027 notes, resulting in a gain of $70 million in the quarter;
- Completed the sales of certain assets which resulted in approximately $680 million in cash proceeds in the third quarter, representing an aggregate $158 million gain; and
- Paid a regular quarterly dividend of $0.09 per share in October 2026.


Edward K. Aldag, Jr., Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, said, “Our results this quarter demonstrate the decisive steps we have taken to strengthen our balance sheet and create greater flexibility to further reduce debt and pursue selective growth opportunities. As healthcare providers around the world seek new solutions to capital challenges, our business model is more important than ever and we are well positioned to create long-term value for our shareholders.


“We are closely monitoring operations at HSA as they navigate continued revenue cycle management challenges that precluded payment of September rent, reducing our NFFO by two cents during the quarter. HSA recently engaged a leading management services provider, Ovation Healthcare, to oversee operations across the portfolio and improve billings and collections.”


Included in the financial tables accompanying this press release is information about the Company’s assets and liabilities, operating results, and reconciliations of net income (loss) to NFFO, including per share amounts, all on a basis comparable to 2025 results.


**PORTFOLIO UPDATE**


MPT has total assets of approximately $14.4 billion, including $8.3 billion of general acute facilities, $2.4 billion of behavioral health facilities and $1.6 billion of post-acute facilities. As of September 30, 2026, MPT’s portfolio included 365 properties and approximately 37,000 licensed beds leased to or mortgaged by 52 hospital operating companies across the United States, as well as in the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Germany, Spain, Finland, Colombia, Italy and Portugal.


As previously disclosed, during the quarter, the Company sold its remaining interest in five hospitals in Utah for approximately $174 million. Additionally, the Company sold its interest in the real estate of two hospitals in Idaho to affiliates of Intermountain Health, an investment grade not-for-profit healthcare system, for approximately $371 million. The sales prices for each of these transactions significantly exceeded the Company’s original investments, again demonstrating the overall value of its portfolio of hospital real estate. Moreover, these and other recent transactions have provided $680 million in proceeds that are available for repayment of debt and other balance sheet improvement.


The Company continues to expect portfolio cash rents in excess of $1.0 billion in 2027, even after reduction of the rental income associated with assets sold in the third quarter. In addition, this estimate includes conservative assumptions about rental income associated with cash basis tenants, including HSA, which continues to be challenged by revenue collection and for whom the Company has recently provided additional working capital support during the quarter.


**OPERATING RESULTS**


Net income for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $202 million ($0.34 per share), compared to a net loss of ($78 million) (($0.13) per share) in the year earlier period. NFFO for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $64 million ($0.11 per share), compared to $77 million ($0.13 per share) in the year earlier period.

The dial-in numbers for the conference call are 833-461-5787 (Toll-Free) and 585-542-9983, and the Meeting ID is 336661409 to join the conference. **About Medical Properties Trust, Inc.**


Medical Properties Trust, Inc. is a self-advised real estate investment trust formed in 2003 to acquire and develop net-leased hospital facilities. From its inception in Birmingham, Alabama, the Company has grown to become one of the world’s largest owners of hospital real estate with 365 facilities and approximately 37,000 licensed beds in nine countries and across three continents as of September 30, 2026. MPT’s financing model facilitates acquisitions and recapitalizations, and allows operators of hospitals to unlock the value of their real estate assets to fund facility improvements, technology upgrades and other investments in operations. For more information, please visit the Company’s website at **[www.mpt.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.mpt.com&esheet=54630841&newsitemid=20261028521872&lan=en-US&anchor=www.mpt.com&index=3&md5=c1ac557e4e4fbde62c0286b1dfaefd1f)** .

Notes:


Investors and analysts following the real estate industry utilize funds from operations ("FFO") as a supplemental performance measure. FFO, reflecting the assumption that real estate asset values rise or fall with market conditions, principally adjusts for the effects of GAAP depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, which assumes that the value of real estate diminishes predictably over time. We compute FFO in accordance with the definition provided by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts, or Nareit, which represents net income (loss) (computed in accordance with GAAP), excluding gains (losses) on sales of real estate and impairment charges on real estate assets, plus real estate depreciation and amortization, including amortization related to in-place lease intangibles, and after adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures.


In addition to presenting FFO in accordance with the Nareit definition, we disclose normalized FFO, which adjusts FFO for items that relate to unanticipated or non-core events or activities or accounting changes that, if not noted, would make comparison to prior period results and market expectations less meaningful to investors and analysts. We believe that the use of FFO, combined with the required GAAP presentations, improves the understanding of our operating results among investors and the use of normalized FFO makes comparisons of our operating results with prior periods and other companies more meaningful. While FFO and normalized FFO are relevant and widely used supplemental measures of operating and financial performance of REITs, they should not be viewed as a substitute measure of our operating performance since the measures do not reflect either depreciation and amortization costs or the level of capital expenditures and leasing costs (if any not paid by our tenants) to maintain the operating performance of our properties, which can be significant economic costs that could materially impact our results of operations. FFO and normalized FFO should not be considered an alternative to net income (loss) (computed in accordance with GAAP) as indicators of our results of operations or to cash flow from operating activities (computed in accordance with GAAP) as an indicator of our liquidity.


Certain line items above (such as depreciation and amortization) include our share of such income/expense from unconsolidated joint ventures. These amounts are included with all activity of our equity interests in the "Earnings from equity interests" line on the consolidated statements of income.


(A) Total share-based compensation expense is $0.4 million and $12.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $5.8 million and $30.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, (including certain awards that are to be settled in cash). Cash-settled awards are typically recorded in accordance with GAAP at fair value and remeasured at each balance sheet date until settlement. The resulting fluctuations, which are primarily driven by changes in our stock price rather than operational performance, can introduce significant volatility in our earnings. To enhance comparability and provide a more stable view of performance over time, NFFO reflects additional expense of $8.1 million and a benefit of $3.5 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and additional expense of $21.4 million and a benefit of $3.4 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, to arrive at total share-based compensation expense using grant date fair value for all awards (including cash-settled awards) of $8.5 million and $8.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $27.2 million and $27.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.


(B) Includes revenue accrued during the period but not received in cash, such as deferred rent, payment-in-kind ("PIK") interest or other accruals.


(C) Includes cash received to satisfy previously accrued non-cash revenue, such as the cash receipt of previously deferred rent or PIK interest.
